rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The followers mean that the leaders came from every side to keep them from hearing the Prophet's message.
rows.anchor: you people would come to us from the right and left to stop us from listening to what the Prophet (sws) has to say to us.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders interrupt the followers before they finish, declaring themselves acquitted; the discourse itself portrays this intervention.
rows.anchor: leaders will not even let their followers who are blindly following them complete their sentence; they will interject and declare their own acquittal.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word sultān means force or authority: the leaders deny they could forcibly prevent faith and blame the followers for disobedience and arrogance after truth became clear.
rows.anchor: The word انَطْلُسٌ means “force and authority”.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders say both groups are sinners, God's announced response to Satan's challenge has come true, and they must taste the punishment.
rows.anchor: the prediction of God that He had made in response to the challenge of Satan has materialized

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders argue they would be culpable for making others evil only if they themselves were virtuous; followers lacked judgment in following them and show still worse judgment by blaming them.
rows.anchor: We would have been blameworthy if we were virtuous and we wanted to make you evil; we tried to make you like us

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blind following makes people go astray: those who set aside intellect and intention cannot succeed in God's test of both.
rows.anchor: a person who sends his intellect and intention into abeyance will never succeed in this trial.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun meaning before them refers to the Quraysh, and the discourse turns to historical arguments.
rows.anchor: The antecedent of the pronoun in ْمُهَلْبَق is “the Quraysh”.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier nations also went astray: God sent warners from among them, but they followed their forefathers blindly and met the consequence after truth was conclusively conveyed.
rows.anchor: many other nations had gone astray earlier and met their fate.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only servants chosen by God's mercy escaped that fate; this reassures the Prophet to persevere and leave the Quraysh's matter to God.
rows.anchor: Only those of God’s servants were protected from this evil fate whom God’s mercy had chosen

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophet narratives share a refrain of God's peace and mercy, support for the messenger's mission, and reward for good deeds; this refrain summarizes the anecdotes.
rows.anchor: It is this motif which, in fact, is the summary of these anecdotes as well.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Through Aaron, the prophets are listed chronologically; afterward their order follows each prophet's attributes.
rows.anchor: Till the mention of Aaron (sws) all prophets are cited in the chronological order; after that the sequence is based on the attributes

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's prayer followed a very long preaching effort after he had lost hope; the author connects it with his supplication in Sūrah Shuʿarāʾ and the detailed invocation in Sūrah Nūḥ.
rows.anchor: This is a reference to the supplication made by Noah (sws) before his Lord

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Noah's exhausted plea, God answered at once: all except the believers were drowned; Nūḥ also describes their drowning and subsequent fire, with no helpers.
rows.anchor: Hence, his pleading was answered by God forthwith.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah's story assures the Prophet and companions to endure hardship patiently: God hears their prayers and efforts, and will aid them and rout their enemies once the truth is conclusively delivered.
rows.anchor: The verse under discussion is meant to assure the Prophet (sws) and his companions; they should bear adverse circumstances with patience

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author takes Noah's ahl to mean his family and clan members who believed.
rows.anchor: refers to all his family and clan who had embraced faith.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He notes that ahl can also refer to a person's followers.
rows.anchor: Though this word can also refer to the followers of a person

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the few among Noah's descendants who believed survived the flood, and the later world was populated through them.
rows.anchor: it was these who remained alive after the deluge and the world was populated through them later

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic suppresses a governing noun and the verb's object; restoring them yields the sense that God left a group from later generations on Noah's way.
rows.anchor: a governing noun ( mud@āf) and the object of the verb اَنْكَرَت is suppressed as per the linguistic principles of Arabic.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surviving later group alludes to Noah's preaching mission succeeding despite his enemies' hostility.
rows.anchor: This is an allusion to the success of his preaching mission: in spite of the animosity of his enemies
